svg.data-input: AC 200 to 240V, 16A max x2; DC -40 to -72V, 80A max x2
svg.data-optics-qsfp-dd: 800GE QSFP-DD OpenZR+/ZR/2xLR4/2xFR4/DR8+/DR8/SR8; 400GE QSFP-DD OpenZR+/ZR/ER4/LR4/FR4/SR8/DR4/DR4+/PLR4; 200GE QSFP56 SR4/FR4; 100GE QSFP28 ZR4/ER4/SR4/LR4 (datasheet Compatible Transceivers). Per-port optical power is budgeted 16 W on ports 0-31 and 23 W on ports 32-63 (HIG Figure 9 note)
svg.data-optics-sfp28: 1G/10G/25G SFP28 up to 40 km (HIG Port Overview table, ports 64-65; the datasheet's Compatible Transceivers list covers only the QSFP-DD field)
svg.data-timing: Stratum 3E OCXO; SyncE; IEEE 1588v2 (default, G.8265.1, G.8275.1, G.8275.2); T-TC, T-BC/OC, T-GM
svg.data-console: RJ45 RS-232 and micro-USB, both labelled IOIO, 115200 8N1 (micro-USB needs the Silicon Labs CP210x driver)
svg.data-timing-inputs: 1x 1PPS in/out SMB and 1x 10MHz in/out SMB, both Premium-build only
svg.data-emc: FCC Part 15 Subpart B Class A; ICES-003 Class A; EN 55032 Class A; EN 300 386; EN 55035; VCCI CISPR 32 Class A
svg.data-nebs: NEBS statements only (Common Bonding Network suitability, GR-1089 intra-building port restriction, external SPD required on AC) - the HIG prints the compliance statements without claiming a NEBS level, and none is claimed here

Broadcom Tomahawk5 BCM78900 at 51.2 Tbps, Intel Ice Lake-D 4-core with an AST2620 BMC, 1+1 hot-swap 3000W AC or DC PSUs, 3+1 hot-swap fans, front-to-back airflow","format":1,"gaps":[{"note":"Five plain round features sit on the front panel and no HIG callout names any of them. The one this entry was opened for is a third round opening the size of the two SMB timing bezels, directly above them at (6.79, 32.9), 6.8 mm across, drawn black where they are yellow; the datasheet lists only two timing interfaces and no held image resolves what is behind it. The other four are a 3.7 mm disc left of the RESET pinhole at (12.75, 9.35), a 3.0 mm disc right of the ID legend box at (18.6, 31.0), and two 6.6 mm openings with a lighter rim at the right edge, (430.8, 21.4) and (430.6, 66.4), flanking the rounded slot between them - plausibly rail or handle furniture on a chassis that hangs on inner rails, but the HIG's rail section draws the SIDE pins and never this face. All five are measured from the vendor front render and drawn as dark decor circles, so the panel is not silently missing a hole, and all five are named here so they are recorded unknowns rather than stray marks.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["furniture"],"wanted":"a photograph of the front panel's timing column, or a mechanical drawing of the front bezel.","what":"unidentified-front-panel-opening"},{"note":"every one of the 64 QSFP-DD ports and both SFP28 ports carries a lamp on the strip beside it, and the HIG's front-panel LED section defines only the six system lamps (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID) plus the management port pair. It gives no colour vocabulary at all for the port lamps, so the 66 placements here carry positions and no states.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["port-leds"],"wanted":"a NOS LED table, or photographs of a live unit with known ports up and down.","what":"qsfp-dd-port-led-semantics"},{"note":"the five system lamps and the ID lamp each sit beside a printed white legend box, but the best resolution the intake reaches on that block is HIG Figure 8 at 8.6 px/mm over an embedded raster of far less, where the glyphs are a grey smear. The terminal block's size and position on the face are the weakest numbers in this model. The AC unit's face is measured; the DC one's is not, and the two must not be read as equally sourced.","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["psus"],"wanted":"a straight-on drawing or photograph of the PSU-302-DESR face.","what":"dc-psu-face-not-measured"},{"note":"'FAN 0 1 2 3' is printed once on the chassis strip between the fan bank and the PSUs, which is modelled - but it is a single legend naming four bays rather than a per-bay mark, so nothing on the drawing ties bay 2 to the digit 2. Whether the hardware also prints a digit on or beside each bay is not resolvable from the elevation, where the fan modules cover whatever is behind them.","reason":"needs-hardware","scope":["fans"],"wanted":"a photograph of the rear with one or more fan modules removed.","what":"fan-position-legends"},{"note":"ufispace/fan-808012 states no draw and its own contract records the search: the datasheet names FAN-808012-HCE only as an ordering line, and the HIG dimensions the fan FRU, weighs it and tables its LED without a wattage. Every watt figure in either document belongs to the PSU ordering lines or to the two system maxima. L29's standing warning is the live count of how much of the chassis total is a floor rather than a total.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["fans"],"wanted":"a photograph of the fan module's label, or a UfiSpace FRU datasheet.","what":"fru-power-unpublished"},{"note":"the S9321-64EO is the same chassis with 64 OSFP cages instead of QSFP-DD, drawn beside this device on the same HIG page, and it is a different left-cluster layout as well (its 1PPS and 10MHz sit above the model name, its console block below). It is not modelled here for two reasons worth separating: it is a different SKU with its own weight and its own per-port power split (16 red ports at 30 W, 48 at 16 W, against this device's 32/32 at 16 and 23 W), and the library has no std/osfp cage to seat in it.","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["qsfpdd-800g"],"wanted":"an OSFP cage in std/, sized from the OSFP MSA.","what":"osfp-sibling-not-modelled"}],"groups":{"fans":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"3+1","redundancy-note":"3+1 - 3+1 hot-swap fans (the device description)"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Point"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the management and timing cluster at the left-hand end - OOB RJ45, USB-A, RJ45 and micro-USB console, 1PPS and 10MHz SMB - plus the RESET button","role":"management","term":"Port"},"port-leds":{"description":"one lamp per traffic port - 32 on the strip above the upper QSFP-DD band, 32 on the strip below the lower one, and a pair under the SFP28 legend","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"psus":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"1+1 redundant, hot-swappable, active-active"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"qsfpdd-800g":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp-dd","speed":"800g"},"description":"the 64 200/400/800G QSFP-DD ports, 0-63, in two bands of 16 columns x 2 belly-to-belly rows; ports 0-31 are budgeted at 16 W of optics and 32-63 at 23 W","index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"sfp28":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp28","speed":"25g"},"description":"the two 10/25G SFP28 management uplinks, stacked in one ganged shell left of the QSFP-DD field; the vendor numbers them 64 and 65, continuing the QSFP-DD range rather than restarting, which is what rel-pos carries","index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"status-leds":{"description":"the six front-panel system lamps - SYNC SYS FAN PS0 PS1 in a column beside their legend box, and ID standing alone higher up the panel","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"UfiSpace","maturity":"modelled","model":"S9321-64E","name":"s9321-64e","portfolio":{"also-listed-in":["Cloud & Data Centers"],"family":"Datacenter Switch for AI/ML","line":"AI Networking"},"provenance":{"attrs":"datasheet Specifications table and Available to Order section, with the HIG's two Connecting Power sections for the system maxima and its Preparation Check List for the input currents. The timing rows are marked '(Premium)' by the vendor and that qualifier is carried into the attr rather than dropped, because it is the difference between a feature this SKU has and one an order has to ask for.","blanked-opening":"UNIDENTIFIED, recorded not resolved. A third round opening the same size as the two SMB bezels sits directly above them at (6.79, 32.9), 6.8 mm across, drawn black where they are yellow and carrying no printed legend - the '1PPS' text below it belongs to the jack below that. HIG Figure 4 calls out only 1PPS and 10MHz in that column and the datasheet lists only two timing interfaces, both '(Premium)'. It is drawn as a dark decor circle and named in gaps; guessing it into a port would be inventing a connector.","bottom":"deliberately size-only - no photograph or drawing of the underside exists in the intake. HIG Figure 4 shows top, front and rear; Figures 10-13 show the chassis from above and from the front-left on rails; Figures 20-22 show the rear grounding pad. Nothing looks at the base, and inventing the label field this class of device usually carries would be a guess. L45's size-only warning stands as the record.","buttons":"drawing - HIG Figure 4's 'Reset' callout points at a single recessed circular button whose ring centres (20.6, 9.3) and measures 1.7 mm across; drawn with common/reset-button (4 mm recessed pinhole, the nearest library part) with its printed RESET legend above it, which is where the artwork puts it. There is no Mode button on this platform - the HIG front-panel LED table defines no mode-switched lamp.","chassis":"datasheet - 'Chassis (W x D x H) 2RU, 436 x 762 x 87.7 mm or 17.17\" x 30\" x 3.45\" Weight: 23.72 kg or 52.28 lbs (Without FRU)'; the HIG Component Physical Information table repeats all three ('S9321-64E/EO (W x D x H) 17.16' x 30' x 3.45' (436 x 762 x 87.7mm)', 'Chassis without FRU S9321-64E: 52.28lbs(23.72kg)'). 436 is the body between the rail folds, not a rack face: the HIG Space Clearance section separates 'The S9321-64E/EO chassis width is 17.16 inches (43.6cm)' from the 'adjustable mounting rail kit suited for standard 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks', and this chassis has no bolt-on ears at all - it hangs on inner rails that clip to five standoff pins per side - so there is no ear extent to subtract. HIG Figure 8's elevation shows two small stubs projecting beyond the body at the left; those are rail furniture and are not drawn. Depth 762 is likewise without the FRUs; the fan handle projects 29 mm and the PSU handle 30 mm beyond it (HIG Space Clearance), carried as relief on the FRU contracts rather than in the chassis depth.","front-layout":"drawing - HIG Figure 8, the S9321-64E front elevation (the S9321-64EO drawn below it on the same page is the OSFP sibling and is NOT this device), rendered from the PDF at 600 dpi. GATE 1: the chassis in it measures 3759 x 763 px, aspect 4.927 against the datasheet's 4.971 (436/87.7) - 0.9% out, so it is orthographic and carries geometry at 8.622 px/mm across. Vertical readings are corrected by 87.7/88.5 for the residual 0.9%, and that correction is why the y numbers below are quoted to a tenth and not a hundredth.","fru-parts":"three components were built for this device because nothing in the library fitted: ufispace/fan-808012 (FAN-808012-HCE, 81 x 81.5 - the existing fan-402825 is 51.5 x 42.2 and fan-405637 is a different family again), ufispace/psu-302-ac and ufispace/psu-302-dc (PSU-302-AESR / -DESR, 68 x 40.6 at 3000 W - the library's UfiSpace PSUs run 132 to 921 W in faces from 50.5 to 73 mm wide and none is this envelope). Checked std/ and common/ first: std/qsfp-dd, std/sfp-ganged, std/smb, std/micro-usb, std/usb-a, std/rj45-ganged, std/c20-inlet, common/led-dot, common/reset-button, common/ground-symbol, common/usb-symbol and common/screw-head all fitted and are reused. There is no std/osfp in the library, which is one reason the OSFP sibling S9321-64EO is not modelled here.","left-cluster":"drawing - HIG Figure 8 at 8.622 px/mm, with HIG Figure 4's callouts naming every part of it: Reset, ID LED, 1PPS, 10MHz, System LED, RJ45 OOB, USB 3.0, RJ45 Console Ports, Micro USB Console Ports. Measured: the recessed RESET ring centres (20.6, 9.3); the ID lamp is cyan at (13.59, 28.11) with its white 'ID' legend box at x 15.08-17.28; the two yellow SMB bezels centre (9.29, 43.19) and (9.29, 57.07) at 7.3 mm across, each under its own printed legend; the five system lamps run down x 11.08 at y 64.18 / 66.34 / 68.88 / 71.35 / 73.91 beside a white legend box at x 12.87-17.51, y 64.25-74.48. Those five measured gaps are 2.16 / 2.54 / 2.47 / 2.56 and they are drawn on an even 2.43 pitch instead: a lamp block on one centreline, with the drawing's 0.15 mm scatter recorded here rather than copied. The silver bezel plate holding the OOB jack, the USB-A and the console jack measures x 19.25-34.91, y 46.78-77.70, and its two internal rails at y 57.5-59.8 and 64.9-67.4 divide it into the three openings the parts are seated in. The management and console jacks are drawn with std/rj45-ganged because the plate is one piece of metal 15.7 mm wide - a 16 mm single-port IEC bezel does not fit it. The SMB jacks are std/smb (4.83 mm, registry) seated on the measured centres with the yellow bezel ring drawn as decor behind them, because the registry sizes the connector and the 7.3 mm yellow is the washer around it.","lifecycle":"searched 2026-08-28, 'UfiSpace S9321-64E end of life' - no announcement. The vendor lists the product as current and it is a 2024-generation Tomahawk5 platform. none-announced is a checked state, not an absence.","port-grid":"measured - and the RULER IS THE LAMPS, not the shells. The 32 per-port lamps on the strip above the field give column centres 70.10, 93.06, 116.01 ... 414.45, a uniform pitch of 22.957 over fifteen steps (individual steps 22.90-23.05). The eight ganged shells' own drawn edges give block steps of 47.6 / 45.2 / 46.5 / 46.3 / 44.5 / 47.3 / 45.8 - a +/-1.6 mm scatter about 2 x 22.957 = 45.91, which no real cage assembly has and which three independent bands of the same figure reproduce identically. So the shells are derived from the lamp grid rather than measured, and the two agree end to end: the shells' measured span 58.34-426.03 is 367.69 against the grid's 367.31, 0.4 mm over 368. THE SHELL EDGES IN THIS FILE ARE THEREFORE COMPUTED, NOT READ - said here because they look measured.","port-leds":"measured - one lamp per port, 32 on the strip above the upper band at y centre 10.13 and 32 on the strip below the lower band at y centre 82.10, each 1.5 mm across in the drawing. Their x positions are the port grid's own ruler (see port-grid): the lamp for port 2j sits at 63.30 + 22.957j and the lamp for port 2j+1 at 76.90 + 22.957j, so a column's pair straddles a 13.6 mm hex-vent gap with 9.3 mm to the next column's pair. Drawn with common/led-dot (2.0 mm, nearest part). The HIG tables the SYNC/SYS/FAN/PS0/PS1/ID lamps in full and says nothing about what the per-port lamps show, so they carry no states - see gaps.","port-numbering":"HIG Port Overview table: 'Port ID 0~63 QSFP-DD or OSFP ... 64~65 SFP28', and HIG Figure 8 prints large blue numerals across the cages as a schematic aid. Those numerals are guide art - the vendor front render s9321-64e-2-view.png shows bare cages - so what is modelled is the strip the real device prints: read at 4x zoom it runs '0\u25b2 (lamp) ... (lamp) 1\u25bc 2\u25b2 (lamp) ... (lamp) 3\u25bc', a numeral and an arrow at each end of every column with that column's two lamps inboard of them. \u25b2 is the upper row of the band and \u25bc the lower, on both strips, so the bottom strip reads '32\u25b2 ... 33\u25bc 34\u25b2'. Column j therefore carries ports 2j and 2j+1 in the top band and 32+2j / 33+2j in the bottom one, which is what the big numerals also say.","port-rows":"drawing - the 64 cages sit in two bands of 16 columns x 2 rows. Each band's ganged shell runs y 14.7-43.8 and 49.3-78.4 (both 29.1 tall, an even 34.6 apart), and within a band the two cage rows are belly-to-belly with their gaskets meeting in a bright seam at y 28.5-30.0. READING THE ROW PITCH OFF THE GUIDE'S GREY FILLS IS THE TRAP HERE, and the first pass fell into it: those fills are the module faces (y 16.4-24.3 and 33.6-41.7, centres 17.3 apart), and each port also owns the EMI gasket band on its inboard side (24.4-28.4 above the seam, 30.1-33.5 below it). Port for port that is 16.4-28.4 and 30.1-41.7, centres 22.4 and 35.9, a pitch of 13.5 - and the 17.3 version put a 7 mm gap down the middle of every block that the reference does not have, which is what the matched-scale comparison showed and nothing else would have. std/qsfp-dd's registry 19.0 x 10.0 opening is seated on the corrected centres; the QSFP-DD MSA governs the opening size and the figure does not. The upper row of each band is rotate 180 so its cage lip faces the seam, as both rows do on the hardware and as the figure draws them.","power":"datasheet gives 'Typical power: 913 Watts (no transceiver)'. The HIG's two Connecting Power sections give the maxima with the testing criteria printed beside them - 40C ambient, optics fully populated, 100% traffic load - hence power-envelope: fully-configured. They differ by input type, not by measure or scope: 'The maximum system power consumption is 2496 watts' (DC Version) and 'The maximum system power consumption is 2589 watts' (AC Version). Two variants of one box, not a source disagreement, so both are carried - power-max-w takes the higher AC figure and power-max-dc-w the DC one. Per-port optical budgets are stated under HIG Figure 9 and belong to this SKU specifically: 'S9321-64E: The upper 32 ports support 16W, while the bottom 32 ports support 23W' - the OSFP sibling's split is different and is not carried here. The vendor qualifies every one of these figures; nothing here is an unqualified reading.","rear-layout":"photo-measured+drawing - the vendor rear render s9321-64e-3-rear.png (507 x 102 px for the chassis, aspect 4.971 against a true 4.971 - EXACT, but only 1.163 px/mm) and HIG Figure 4's rear elevation rendered at 600 dpi (1593 x 320 px, aspect 4.978, 0.1% out, 3.654 px/mm), which is the one the numbers come from. Four fan modules on a step of 84.3 mm: the step is a cross-correlation of the two identical middle modules (correlation 0.983) and it is corroborated three more ways - the module seams give 84.0, the red handles 84.4, the red 'E' badges 84.7, and the four lit status lamps in the photograph 84.2. An eyeball read of the same image gave 51.3 on the S6301 and was wrong, which is why none of these is an eyeball read. The module faces measure 83.2 wide against the HIG component table's 81 - a flange, not a disagreement, and the table's figure is what the bays and the component carry. Grounding column between the fans and the PSUs: two M4 holes at (350.1, 11.6) and (350.1, 27.8) with the earth symbol below at (350.4, 51.0), which is the HIG's one stated lug location ('located on the rear of the router'). The two PSU bays are stacked, not side by side: face x 360.0-428.0 measured against the drawing's sharp seam at 359.5, width 68.0 exactly as the HIG dimension drawing states, y 3.3 and 45.7 for a measured 40.5 face against the drawing's dimensioned 40.6.","round-panel-features":"drawing - the front carries five plain round features that no HIG callout names, and they are listed here so none of them reads as a stray mark. Measured on the vendor front render (chassis x 9-510, y 25-125 px for 436 x 87.7 mm, aspect 4.970 against a true 4.971): a 3.7 mm dark disc left of the RESET pinhole centred (12.75, 9.35); a 3.0 mm dark disc right of the ID legend box centred (18.6, 31.0); the 6.8 mm blanked opening above the two SMB timing bezels centred (6.79, 32.9), which has its own entry; and two 6.6 mm dark openings with a lighter rim at the right-hand edge, centred (430.8, 21.4) and (430.6, 66.4), one above and one below the 2.4 x 27.1 mm rounded slot between them. All five are on the vendor artwork and all five are drawn. Only the timing-column one is identified even negatively - see the unidentified-front-panel-opening gap, which now covers the other four as well.","sfp28-block":"drawing - the two SFP28 management uplinks sit in one 2x1 stacked ganged shell between the left cluster and the QSFP-DD field: shell x 40.83-56.25, y 30.57-62.30 measured as a grey mask on HIG Figure 8. The two ports are seated belly-to-belly on the std/sfp-ganged 15.0 row pitch, at the aperture centres the figure's own yellow '64' and '65' numerals sit on (38.8 and 54.4, a 15.6 pitch - the standard and the figure agree to 0.6 mm). A yellow legend strip above the shell (x 40.9, y 24.4, 15.7 x 2.9) prints '64\u25b2 \u25bc65', with the two port lamps below it at (45.83, 28.58) and (51.68, 28.53).","sides":"estimated - no orthographic side elevation exists in the intake. What does exist is HIG Figure 11's isometric of the inner rail going on, with the five standoff pins numbered 1-5 along the chassis side and the M4 screw hole marked (a) behind them, and the HIG text that fixes the count: 'The chassis has 5 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 10 pins' and 'lock the inner rail to the chassis using two M4 screws (one on each chassis side)'. So the COUNT is the vendor's and the SPACING is mine, laid out evenly over the middle of the 762 mm depth from the isometric's proportions. AXIS CONVENTION: on the RIGHT view x = 0 is the FRONT; on the LEFT view x = 0 is the REAR (renderer convention), so the left view carries the same pattern mirrored as depth - x - width. The pattern is asymmetric front-to-rear - the screw hole is behind the last pin, not centred - so getting the mirror wrong would be visible here, which is why the convention is written next to the numbers.","system-leds":"drawing+HIG - five lamps in a vertical column beside a printed legend box, plus a sixth, the ID lamp, standing alone higher up the panel next to its own 'ID' box. That is exactly the six the HIG front-panel LED table defines - SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID - and the table's order matches the column top to bottom. Drawn with common/led-dot (2.0 mm, nearest part); states transcribed from the table on each placement. The printed legend strings inside the boxes are a grey smear at every resolution the intake holds, so the table's own names are used - see gaps.","top":"drawing - HIG Figure 4's top view, which carries its own W = 17.17\" (436mm) and D = 30\" (762mm) dimension lines. GATE 1 IS MARGINAL: the drawn cover measures 924 x 1685 px for a 436 x 762 object, aspect 0.548 against a true 0.572, 4.2% out - so fractions along each axis are taken and anchored to the dimensioned 436 and 762, and no absolute scale is used. Six recessed stiffening grooves on a 95.2 mm pitch, centres at y 192 / 288 / 383 / 478 / 572 / 668 from the rear, each spanning x 15.7-416.8. Cover screws are placed from the same fractions to about a millimetre.
